correctness.rationale: The facet areas give the incenter exactly as \(I=(0,t,t)\) with \(t=ph/(L+p+h)\), while centroid and circumcenter follow by direct averaging and equidistance. The collinearity determinant factors into \((p-h)Q\). With \(x=p+h\), \(y=ph\), the equation \(Q=0\) reduces, after a sign-controlled squaring, to \(x^2=4y(y+2)^2/(5y+6)\). The quadratic discriminant then forces \(y\ge2\), and the reconstructed left side is strictly positive, so no extraneous squared solutions survive. The explicit \(y=3\) example satisfies the branch exactly, has center ratio \(-3/5\), and has a nonperpendicular pair of opposite edges, so it is non-orthocentric; its edge multiset rules out every biregular partition.

value.rationale: The motivating literature poses a broad geometric characterization problem and identifies the orthocentric/biregular case as the only known regime. The present family is not an arbitrary numerical slice: after fixing one edge by similarity, it is the simplest two-parameter tetrahedron with a reflection symmetry and two symmetry-fixed vertices on perpendicular axes, which makes all three centers exactly tractable while retaining nonorthocentric shapes. A complete algebraic classification inside this family and a continuous nonorthocentric branch provide a concrete structural boundary for any future global characterization. The exact witness shows that orthocentric/biregular models cannot exhaust the solution set.
